meta.title: Website in 5 minutes
meta.by: Langara College, Department of Design Formation
meta.note: Single source of truth for the game. The Figma file is the visual reference; this file is what the code reads.

flow.notes: Shown after 60s idle. Clients take turns speaking (3.5s each). Silent until first tap.
Arrow keys browse, Enter picks. 'Surprise me' picks a random client not played this session.
Client speaks the brief (voice + bubble). Timer starts on 'Start building'.
Tabs: Colour, Type, Style, Images, Decor. 'Send to <client>' any time.
At 0:00 the Deadline appears and sends the site exactly as it is.

kit.paletteContrastNote: All text pairs pass WCAG AA in every palette. Text on accent uses onAccent; text on accent2 uses onAccent2; accent-coloured text uses accentText.

styles.name: Classic
styles.description: Small radius, hairline border, light shadow

styles.name: Soft & Rounded
styles.description: Big radius, no border, soft shadow

styles.name: Neo-Brutalist
styles.description: Square, thick border, hard offset shadow

styles.name: Playful
styles.description: Pill buttons, chunky outline, colour sticker shadow

kit.picturesNote: Photo pictures are placeholders in Figma. Use real licensed photos (e.g. Adobe Stock) or keep the placeholder card. Decoys are worth 0 for everyone.
kit.sectionPatternsNote: Patterns sit behind Features, Stats, Testimonial, Pricing, Team, FAQ and About at about 12% opacity in the palette's border or accent2 colour.
kit.sectionsNote: On phones every multi-column section collapses to 1 column (2 for gallery/team). The player's column choice applies from 768px up.

decoration.note: +1 only if the hero decor AND every section pattern used are on the client's lists

everyonesRules.breaksWhen: Navigation is not the top section
everyonesRules.comment: Where’s the menu? I’m lost on my own website.

everyonesRules.breaksWhen: Footer is not the bottom section
everyonesRules.comment: Why is the footer in the middle? Is the website falling over?
What is this website even for?
Is that it? I’ve seen longer receipts.
I scrolled so long I needed a snack.
I need my glasses for this. All of them.

everyonesRules.breaksWhen: Confetti or Sparkles together with Checks or Stripes
everyonesRules.comment: My eyes! Everything is happening at once!

everyonesRules.breaksWhen: Same section type 3 times in a row
everyonesRules.comment: Didn’t I just see this? And this? And this?

scoring.rulesNote: Score never goes below 0. Each broken rule triggers its comment once (as a live bubble).

dealBreaker.label: Deal-breaker!
dealBreaker.note: Bar drops to 0, face goes to meltdown, recovers when removed

clients.name: Gerald Ledgerby
clients.personality: Has ironed his socks. Owns three calculators and has given each of them a name.
clients.brief: My clients trust me with their money. I’d like a website that makes them feel… calm. Nothing should move. Nothing should sparkle. Last year someone sent me an emoji and I had to lie down.
clients.lesson: Serif type and navy read as established and trustworthy. That is why banks and law firms use them. Neon and sparkles say “fun”, not “safe with your money”.

hero.title: Your taxes, handled precisely
hero.body: Thirty-one years of accurate returns and absolutely zero surprises.

features.title: How I can help
items: Filed on time, every time, triple-checked.
I bring the binders. You bring the coffee.

quotes: Gerald found $412 I didn’t know I had. I cried a little, in a good way.

faq.title: Questions, answered
items: What do I need to bring?
Last year’s return, your slips and any receipts. I’ll send a checklist.
Can you help with last year’s return?
Yes, and the year before. I enjoy that sort of thing.
Do you accept receipts in a shoebox?
I do. I don’t enjoy it, but I do.

contact.title: Book a consultation
contact.body: Tell me what you need and I’ll reply within one business day.

about.title: Thirty-one years of tidy books
about.body: I started Ledgerby Tax with one desk and three calculators. I still have all three.

footer.note: © 2026 Ledgerby Tax & Accounting. Weekdays 9–5, never on weekends.

happy: This is… orderly. I may frame it. Next to my other framed spreadsheet.
Balanced, like a good ledger. I’m experiencing what young people call “a vibe”.
My clients will trust this. I trust this. I’m emailing my mother.
meh: It’s fine. Like a tie that’s slightly too wide. I’ll live.
It mostly adds up. There’s a rounding error somewhere and it’s bothering me.
meltdown: Why is it SPARKLING? My glasses just fogged up.
This website owes me an apology and possibly back taxes.
I need a quiet room, a pencil and a glass of room-temperature water.
lines.timesUp: Late? I have never filed anything late in thirty-one years.
lines.hurry: Thirty seconds. I’m getting my calculator out.

triggers.perfectPalette: Navy. The colour of reliable socks. Go on.
triggers.dealBreakerPalette: Is my screen broken or is this… pink?
triggers.perfectHeading: A serif! Finally, a font with a pension plan.
triggers.dealBreakerHeading: That font looks like it would bounce a cheque.
triggers.perfectStyle: Neat edges. Tidy borders. I feel audited in a good way.
triggers.decoyPicture: Who chose this picture? It isn’t itemised.
triggers.dealBreakerDecoration: Is something… celebrating? Make it stop.
triggers.mustHaveAdded: Ah, Margaret’s review. She’s very thorough.

clients.name: Kaia Zoom
clients.business: Leafr, a dating app, but for ferns
clients.personality: Has pivoted four times this week. Says “disrupt” the way other people say “hello”.
clients.brief: Okay so Leafr matches houseplants with their soulmates. We’re pre-revenue but post-vibes. The site has to feel LOUD. If it looks like a bank, investors fall asleep, and honestly that’s on you.
clients.lesson: Saturated colour on a dark background and chunky sans-serifs feel young and energetic. Classic serifs signal tradition, the opposite of a startup pitch.

hero.title: Swipe right on houseplants
hero.body: The dating app that finally matches you with a fern that gets you.

features.title: Why Leafr?
items: Our algorithm knows your light levels, your watering habits and your vibe.
Ghost a cactus. It won’t text back.

testimonial.title: Plant parents say
quotes: I matched with a monstera and we’re moving in together.
My snake plant finally feels understood.
Better than my last three apps combined.

pricing.title: Pick your plan
plans: A tiny hat for your cactus

about.title: Founded in a greenhouse at 3am
about.body: Kaia was lonely. Her fern was lonely. The rest is history (and a pitch deck).

faq.title: FAQ
items: They lean towards the light. We take that as a yes.

contact.title: Say hi
contact.body: Investors, plant parents, curious cacti: we read everything.

happy: OBSESSED. This is going in the pitch deck. You’re getting equity. (You’re not getting equity.)
This slaps. My co-founder is crying. Okay, he cries a lot, but still.
Ten out of ten. Disruptive. Iconic. Already posted it.
meh: It’s giving… Tuesday. Can it be more Friday?
Cute! In a “my aunt made a website” kind of way.
meltdown: Is this a PDF from 2009? My investors just unfollowed me.
This looks like a bank. I’d rather pivot to selling candles.
I’m literally shaking. Not in a good way. In a “call my therapist” way.
lines.timesUp: Missed the deadline? Honestly, very on-brand for a startup.
lines.hurry: Thirty seconds! That’s like three pivots!

triggers.perfectPalette: NEON. Yes. My retinas and I approve.
triggers.dealBreakerPalette: Navy? Are we filing taxes or changing the world?
triggers.perfectHeading: Chunky font energy. Love that for us.
triggers.dealBreakerHeading: That font has a mortgage and a minivan.

triggers.decoyPicture: Is that a stock photo? I can smell the stock photo.

clients.name: Rosa Moretti
clients.personality: Feeds everyone who walks in. Has never used a measuring cup. Guards her nonna’s recipes like state secrets.
clients.brief: My kids say I need a website. Fine. It should feel like my kitchen: warm, cozy, smells like fresh bread. Show the bread! If it looks like a hospital, I’m calling your mother.
clients.lesson: Warm hues (reds, creams, golds) feel inviting and homemade, and a script font feels handwritten. Cool or dark palettes feel clinical or cold.

hero.title: Fresh from the oven
hero.body: Bread, biscotti and unsolicited life advice, every morning at seven.

about.title: Nonna’s recipes, Rosa’s rules
about.body: Every loaf starts with my grandmother’s handwritten recipes and a lot of patience. No shortcuts, no measuring cups, plenty of love.

features.title: Baked today
items: Thirty-six hours and a lot of love.

quotes: Rosa told me I looked tired and gave me a free cannoli. Five stars.

banner.statement: Come hungry. Leave happy. Bring a friend.

faq.title: Questions
items: Can I get the sourdough recipe?
No. But I’ll show you how to knead.

footer.note: © 2026 Rosa’s Bakery. Open 7am until the bread runs out.

happy: Bellissimo! You’re too skinny. Sit, I’m bringing biscotti.
It smells like bread. I don’t know how, but it smells like bread.
My nonna would approve, and she approved of nothing.
meh: Is nice. A little like store-bought bread. Edible, but I notice.
It’s okay. Like soup with no salt. I see you tried.
Good, but where is the bread? People come for the bread!
meltdown: Madonna mia, why is it so DARK? Who died? Open a window!
This looks like a nightclub. I close at six!
I’m calling your mother. Right now. What’s her number?
lines.timesUp: Late? My dough rises faster than you work!
lines.hurry: Hurry, the cornetti are getting cold!

triggers.dealBreakerPalette: Why is it so cold? Put a sweater on this website.

triggers.dealBreakerHeading: That font looks like it has never eaten a carb.

clients.name: Damien Nightshade
clients.business: Wilted & Co., dried and dramatic flowers
clients.personality: Wears black in July. Finds sunshine “a bit much”. Secretly the sweetest person on this list.
clients.brief: Wilted & Co. sells flowers that have accepted their fate. The site must feel like a candlelit parlour at midnight. Show the bouquets. If I see pastel, I will simply… fade away.
clients.lesson: Dark palettes with deep reds create drama and a sense of luxury, and blackletter type carries centuries of gothic mood. Pastels break the spell instantly.

hero.title: Flowers that have accepted their fate
hero.body: Dried, pressed and dramatic arrangements for weddings, funerals and Tuesdays.

about.title: Damien, keeper of petals
about.body: I started drying flowers because I couldn’t bear to throw them away. Now every bouquet gets a second, darker, more interesting life.

quotes: My bouquet was so beautifully gloomy, the wedding guests wept. In a good way.

happy: Exquisitely gloomy. I shed a single tear. It was perfect.
Like a candle in a dark room. I’ve never felt so seen.
I would be buried in this website. Respectfully.
meh: It’s dark, but dark like a car park. Not dark like a poem.
Fine. It’s the beige of black.
meltdown: Pink? CONFETTI? I’ve never been so personally attacked by a website.
This is so cheerful my eyeliner is running.
Who invited balloons to my funeral? I mean shop.
lines.timesUp: Ah. The Deadline. We’ve met before.
lines.hurry: Thirty seconds. Time is fleeting. Like petals.

triggers.perfectHeading: Blackletter. Finally, a font that understands me.
triggers.perfectStyle: Clean, sharp, quiet. Like a well-kept crypt.
triggers.perfectPictures: Dried flowers. They’ve accepted their fate. As have I.
triggers.decoyPicture: Balloons. In my shop. I need to lie down.
triggers.dealBreakerDecoration: Confetti is just glitter’s annoying cousin.
triggers.mustHaveAdded: Show the bouquets, in all their withered glory.

clients.name: Brenda Bloom
clients.personality: Speaks only in a calm whisper. Has a different tea for every emotion.
clients.brief: Breathe in… my clients come to me to slow down. The website should feel like a long exhale: soft, natural, lots of space to list my sessions. Breathe out… and please, no shouting fonts.
clients.lesson: Muted greens and generous white space slow the eye down, and rounded, light type feels gentle. Loud fonts and confetti raise the energy, the opposite of calm.

hero.title: Slow down. You’re doing great.
hero.body: Gentle breathwork and yoga sessions to help you exhale the week.

features.title: Sessions
items: Ten minutes that change your whole day.

quotes: I came in stressed and left so relaxed I forgot where I parked.

faq.title: Gentle questions
items: I’ve never done yoga. Is that okay?
Absolutely. Every session starts with the basics, at your own pace.
Comfy clothes. We have mats, blankets and too much tea.
Can I just come for the tea?
Yes. Breathing is optional but encouraged.

cta.title: Your exhale is waiting.
cta.body: First session is on us. Bring yourself, we’ll bring the tea.

about.title: Hi, I’m Brenda
about.body: I teach people to slow down, one breath at a time.

footer.note: © 2026 Breathe with Brenda. Inhale, exhale, repeat.

happy: Ahh. I can feel my shoulders dropping. This website is a hug.
Breathe in… breathe out… perfect. Namaste, little website.
This is so calm my tea brewed itself.
meh: It’s… nice. My breathing is steady, but my aura is beige.
I’m calm. Mostly. A little bit of my chakra is frowning.
meltdown: Too. Much. Going. On. My chakras are tightening.
This font is shouting at me. Why is it shouting?
I need a retreat from this website. A long one.
lines.timesUp: Rushing is the enemy of peace. And of good websites.
